summary: Final voice pick: DragonHD Diya vs MAI-Voice vs gpt-4o-mini-tts on long Hinglish samples with emotion changes; one blind page; then ship the winner

passages.summary:
I wrote /home/user/Taxila/docs/research/voice/final/passages.mjs. Nothing was rendered, no money was spent, and nothing was committed. Running `node docs/research/voice/final/passages.mjs` passes the file's own self-checks (exit 0).

**What the file contains**
- `PASSAGES`: three long passages, each split into labelled beats, plus one gpt-4o-mini-tts `instructions` string per passage. The instructions describe the emotion arc and never quote a line.
- **P1, maths (5 beats):** warm greeting; thinking aloud through 25 x 12 samosas by breaking 12 into 10 + 2; the child's "I'll eat all twelve" joke, which she laughs along with; a calm return to the point; real surprise when the child answers 24 samosas = छह सौ by doubling. The praise names what the child did.
- **P2, science (5 beats):** quiet wonder that sunlight is about eight minutes old, building to excitement; a clear explanation (तीन लाख km per second, पंद्रह करोड़ km); the child wrongly says the moon makes its own light, and she corrects it calmly and kindly with the mirror-and-torch picture; encouragement.
- **P3, mixed register (7 beats):** an English-heavy opener; fraction and denominator inside Hindi; cold drink split as एक बटा चार litre = ढाई सौ millilitre, with दो बटा आठ as the same amount; Hindi-heavy photosynthesis; a question to the child; a playful cold-drink tease; an English wrap-up.
- **Writing rules followed:** Hindi in Devanagari, English in Latin, every number as a word, no "...", no laugh or tag tokens, and no comparison with other children. Each sentence is one full breath with no chopped fragments.

**Input per engine (builder functions in the file; they make no network calls)**
- **Diya** (`en-IN-Diya:DragonHDLatestNeural`): `diyaSsml()` imports `plainDragonHD` from v4/lines.mjs, so the document has exactly the form of round-3 arm B. That means Hindi runs wrapped in `<lang hi-IN>`, with no break, rate or prosody.
- **No style try for Diya.** en-IN DragonHD has no style list, and the v4 probe measured no effect from `express-as` on Diya, so there is no documented field to try.
- **MAI** (`hi-IN-Priya:MAI-Voice-2.1`, HD): `maiSsml(p, styleList)` wraps each beat in `express-as`, using a preference list per beat.
- **The MAI renderer must fetch Priya's live style list from voices/list first.** `maiSsml` throws if no list is passed. Sending a style that isn't on the voice's list gave HTTP 502 for Arjun before. Only `excited` and `softvoice` are measured as present for Priya; the other styles are candidates. A beat with no matching style is spoken plain. No breaks or prosody, so the arms differ by voice and not by markup.
- **gpt-4o-mini-tts** (2025-12-15 deployment, voice `marin`, which is Asha's character voice): `oaiBody()` sends the text unchanged plus one instructions string per passage. Each string starts with the same accent, listener and register description, then the arc.

**Length (an estimate, not a measurement)**
- The 20 round-3 clips ran at 1.86–3.29 words per second (median about 2.7).
- On that rate: P1 is 210 words (estimated 64–78 s), P2 is 229 words (70–85 s), P3 is 233 words (71–86 s).
- MAI and marin may speak at a different rate, so measure the real duration on the renders.

**Self-checks:** `check()` fails on digits, ellipses, markup characters, written laugh tokens, wording that compares the child with other children, a missing MAI style preference, or a median-rate estimate outside 60–90 s.

**Costs:** about 3,160 characters across the three passages, so roughly $0.07 per engine per take at the prices in SCAN.md. That is well inside the USD 10 cap.

render.summary:
I rendered and screened 3 passages × 3 voices × 3 takes (27 WAVs), plus a script probe and a cost calibration for gpt-4o-mini-tts. Diya passed 9 of 9 takes and gpt-4o-mini-tts passed 6 of 9. MAI-Voice-2.1 passed none, so its three listening files are fallback takes, each marked `no_take_passed` in the manifest. Total Azure spend was about USD 2 against the USD 10 cap: about USD 0.85 for TTS (all 27 takes plus probes, calibration and a few test calls) and about USD 1 for the two STTs (estimated). Nothing was committed or pushed, and no key appears in any output file (I grepped for them).

**Setup**
- **Diya** (`en-IN-Diya:DragonHDLatestNeural`) and **MAI** (`hi-IN-Priya:MAI-Voice-2.1`, HD, Preview) were rendered from Azure Speech in centralindia, the India-near region.
- **gpt-4o-mini-tts** (deployment `gpt-4o-mini-tts`, served model `gpt-4o-mini-tts-2025-12-15`, voice marin) came from eastus2. No India region offers this model; I checked the model catalogue for centralindia and southindia.
- **MAI styles:** Priya's live style list has no friendly, cheerful, calm or empathetic. So by the rule in `passages.mjs`, only `excited` and `softvoice` were used and the other beats were spoken plain. Priya does list happy, joyful and surprised, but they were not in the preference lists, so I did not add them.
- **Devanagari vs Roman Hindi (P1, one render each):** both passed every gate. Devanagari won on the tie-break, with lower WER: 0.062/0.095 against 0.095/0.114 (gpt-transcribe / Azure). Devanagari was then used for all gpt-4o-mini-tts takes.
- **Take rule (fixed before screening):** keep the first take that passes every gate. If none passes, keep the take with the fewest failures, earliest on a tie.
- **Gates:**
  - numbers or English terms missed by both STTs;
  - punctuation read aloud;
  - any internal or leading silence over 1.5 s;
  - truncation: the closing words found by neither STT, no trailing silence, or a beat with under 40% of its words recognised;
  - extra speech;
  - loudness: source true peak above -0.1 dBFS, or the clip can't be normalised to -26 LUFS without the peak going above -2 dBFS.

No take missed a number or English term on both STTs, including "cold drink". No take read punctuation aloud.

**What the screen found**
- **gpt-4o-mini-tts drops the last words of P3.** In all 3 takes the audio stops 0.08–0.10 s after "okay", and the closing "Bye bye!" is never spoken. Both STTs agree.
- **MAI fails on silence and loudness:**
  - **Pauses:** it leaves 1.4–2.6 s gaps at sentence ends, one of 7.5 s in P2 t2. These occur in plain beats too, so the express-as markup is not the cause.
  - **Peaks:** the source audio reaches full scale (1–4 samples at about 0 dBFS). It still normalises to -26 LUFS without trouble.
  - **Speed:** it speaks at only about 2.0 words/s, so its passages run 98–120 s, against Diya's 60–69 s (about 3.5 words/s).
  - **Added words:** both STTs agree that MAI inserts words not in the text, such as "अब बताओ", "तुम", "तो", "बहुत", plus a "छछ" mouth noise. No gate covers this, so I report it separately.
- **The mai P3 t1 truncation (marked *) is a screening artefact.** gpt-transcribe wrote the English beats in Devanagari, which breaks the literal word match. I did not change the gate, and the pick does not depend on it (t2 is kept by rule).
- **Streaming stalls on long passages.** With SSE streaming, gpt-4o-mini-tts stopped after 33.85 s of the full P1 and never finished (n=1). The same request without streaming returned 83.8 s in 12.4 s, so all its renders are non-streamed. This was a single long request. I didn't test whether the plain-audio streaming used in production stalls the same way; production sends short sentences.

**Cost per minute** (billed units over all 9 takes per voice; INR at 88 per USD):

| voice | billed units | USD / min | INR / min | USD / passage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Diya | 12,000 SSML characters at $22/M | 0.0272 | 2.39 | 0.0293 |
| MAI-Voice-2.1 | 10,446 SSML characters at $22/M | 0.0141 | 1.24 | 0.0255 |
| gpt-4o-mini-tts | about 19,622 audio-out tokens at $12/M and about 5,612 text-in tokens at $0.60/M (estimated) | 0.0185 | 1.63 | 0.0265 |

- MAI is cheapest per minute only because it speaks slowly. For the same words, all three cost USD 0.026–0.029 per passage.
- The $22/M rate for MAI assumes it bills on the "Neural HD Text to Speech Characters" meter. MAI is Preview and has no separate retail meter.
- The non-streamed gpt-4o-mini-tts responses return no token counts. The figures come from 5 short streamed calibration calls that did report usage: a median 25.31 audio tokens per second of output (range 25.11–25.80), and a linear fit for input tokens.

**Files** (all in /home/user/Taxila/docs/research/voice/final/)

page.summary:
The blind listening page is built and a headless Chromium test passed all 35 checks. It is not published, and nothing was committed or pushed.

**Clips and codes**
- Each passage has one section with the 3 voices. That makes 9 MP3s, about 8.9 MB with index.html.
- Each MP3 is encoded from the take that `renders/manifest.json` picks. Loudness goes through `encode()`, imported from `v3/blind/build.py` and not copied.
- Output loudness is -26.4 to -26.5 LUFS, with true peak -5.8 to -9.2 dBFS.
- Each voice has one fixed 3-character code used in every section: KV4 is Diya, 7FJ is MAI and P97 is gpt-4o-mini-tts. Only `blind-key.json` holds this mapping.
- Clip codes are new 5-character codes. The test confirmed no clip code appears in the round 2-3 keys and no voice code is the start of one of them.

**Things raters will hear that the screen already found**
- **gpt-4o-mini-tts, P3:** the page prints the closing "Bye bye!" but this voice never says it. That fault is in all 3 takes.
- **MAI:** all three clips are fallback takes that failed the screen. Raters will hear 1.4–2.6 s silences and words that are not in the text.
- Both facts are recorded in `blind-key.json`, not on the page. A new "stops before the end" tick lets raters report the first one.

**Page**
- It reuses round 3's page: the same name gate, a separate saved record per name (`ratings/{userId}/people/{name}`) plus a name list in `ratings/{userId}`, saved ratings merged in before any write, and the "Show my ratings text" fallback.
- Version is `taxila-voice-final/v1` and the storage prefix is `taxila-voice-final:`.
- Each section shows a short English scene, then the full passage text exactly as all 3 engines received it. The build checks it is byte-identical to the passage text.
- Three short italic notes say what the child just said (the samosa joke, the answer "six hundred", the moon idea). The child is never heard and never compared with anyone.
- Section order, voice order within each section and the order of the final pick list are random per rater, and stay the same for that rater on reload.
- The 1–5 score, failure ticks and note for a clip unlock after 80% listened. This is counted as 50 time slices actually played, so seeking past them does not count. Round 3 only checked the furthest position reached.
- Round 3's 11 failure ticks are kept, and 4 are new: "no feeling, even on the joke or surprise", "a word pronounced strangely", "stops before the end" and "long silence".
- There is a note box for each section.
- At the end, "Which voice should be her voice?" is required. It unlocks once all 9 clips are scored, offers Voice KV4 / 7FJ / P97 in the rater's own order, and has a reason box.

**Headless test** (Chromium, 390 px phone, 1280 px desktop and dark mode)
- The test is at `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/ecee9fc1-62f9-5f67-a47d-69ca79d9981a/scratchpad/blindtest.mjs`. It uses a fake db.
- Covered and passing:
  - the name gate;
  - 3 sections and 9 rows, with each voice code once per section;
  - no engine names in the HTML;
  - an earlier saved score, section note and order merged in and written back;
  - one rater's record left untouched by another;
  - seeking to 97% leaves the clip locked, and playing it through at 4x unlocks it;
  - the final pick stays locked until all 9 clips are scored, then is saved with its reason;
  - order stays the same on reload and differed for all 6 test names;
  - switching person brings the right ratings back;
  - the export text;
  - the not-signed-in message;
  - no sideways scrolling and no page errors.
- Not covered: the real claude.ai db, so the access rules were not tested.

No key appears in any of the files. The search covered `index.html`, `blind-key.json`, `build.py` and `page.template.html`.
